title: Dentist pleads guilty to professional misconduct in 23-year-old's death
summary: A Manitoba dentist charged under the provincial dental regulator's code of conduct in relation to the death of Virginia Blatz has pleaded guilty to professional misconduct.

image.caption: Virginia Blatz, 23, died on Nov. 27, 2024, after she went to have her wisdom teeth removed. (Submitted by Dulaney and Victoria Blatz)

blocks.text: A Manitoba dentist charged under the provincial dental regulator's code of conduct in relation to the death of Virginia Blatz has pleaded guilty to professional misconduct.
Virginia Blatz died after going to have her wisdom teeth removed
The dentist admitted during an inquiry hearing panel in Winnipeg on Monday morning that Blatz was given far more anesthetic than recommended.
Blatz, 23, was pronounced dead after she went to see the doctor to get her wisdom teeth removed on Nov. 27, 2024.

The dentist was charged with contravention of the Manitoba Dental Association's code of ethics, including going against the principles to do no harm, to improve the patient's condition and to provide competent care. He was also charged with professional misconduct.
He entered a guilty plea during Monday morning's hearing.
According to an agreed statement of facts, the dentist far exceeded the recommended dose of Articane — a local anesthetic drug typically given to manage pain — when providing care to Blatz.
The family of Virginia Blatz, 23, is suing the dentist. (Submitted by Dulaney and Victoria Blatz)

At time of her death, Virginia weighed about 100 pounds, and the dose given to her on the day of her death exceeded the maximum dosage that she should have been given by about 200 per cent, said an expert report included in the agreed statement of facts.
Her family is suing the dentist, his practice and the corporation that owns and operates the dental centre, alleging the care provided to Blatz was negligent.

Lauren Scott is a Winnipeg-based reporter with CBC Manitoba. They hold a master’s degree in computational and data journalism, and have previously worked for the Hamilton Spectator and The Canadian Press.
